about: Sources for the molecule stories (tours and story sections). Every sentence in a story file points at one or more ids here. 'checked' says what was read on the page and confirmed. Facts about a structure file (chains, residue numbers, bonds, ligands, organism, size) were read from the local .cif with tools/story_cif.py, story_cif_facts.py and story_measure.py.

sources.title: Molecule of the Month: Hemoglobin
sources.checked: Four chains, two alpha and two beta, each with a heme holding an iron atom; oxygen binds reversibly to the iron; first oxygen is hard to add, then binding gets easier; oxygen pulls a histidine under the heme; carbon monoxide replaces oxygen at the heme; sickle cell is glutamate 6 to valine in the beta chain, deoxy hemoglobin sticks into stiff fibers, cells become C or sickle shaped; Max Perutz solved horse hemoglobin (2dhb); 2hhb has no oxygen bound.

sources.title: Molecule of the Month: Insulin
sources.checked: Made in the pancreas, released after meals; tells liver, muscle and fat cells to take glucose out of the blood; made as a longer chain then clipped to two chains; three disulfide bridges; pig insulin (4ins) differs from human by one amino acid, alanine in place of threonine at the end of the chain; impaired insulin leads to diabetes mellitus; hexamer stores the hormone before release; hydrophobic core of leucine and isoleucine.

sources.title: Molecule of the Month: Collagen
sources.checked: About one quarter of the protein in the body; strengthens tendons and supports skin and organs; bones and teeth add mineral to collagen; three chains in a triple helix; every third amino acid is glycine, which fits inside the helix; proline and hydroxyproline fill many other positions; hydroxyproline needs vitamin C, lack of it causes scurvy; each chain is over 1400 amino acids long; in 1cag an alanine replaces a glycine and crowds the neighbouring chains; heated collagen becomes gelatin.

sources.title: Molecule of the Month: Lysozyme
sources.checked: Small enzyme that breaks the carbohydrate chains of bacterial cell walls so bacteria burst; Alexander Fleming discovered it when a drop of mucus killed bacteria; found in hen egg white, tears and mucus; first enzyme to have its structure solved (2lyz); long active site cleft binds the cell wall carbohydrate chain.

sources.title: Molecule of the Month: Myosin
sources.checked: Powers every voluntary and involuntary movement; captures and breaks ATP to make a power stroke; two heavy chains and four light chains; 1b7t contains only part of the molecule, the tail was clipped off, but includes most of the motor domain; about 300 myosins form a thick filament; heads climb actin filaments; release of phosphate powers the stroke, amplified by the lever arm; about 2 trillion myosins to hold up a baseball.

sources.title: Molecule of the Month: Actin
sources.checked: Actin filaments form the cytoskeleton and the ladder myosin climbs; up to 5 percent of the protein in a typical cell; each actin holds an ATP, broken to ADP after joining a filament, ADP actin lets go more easily; treadmilling; phalloidin from the death cap mushroom clogs cells with actin filaments; crystal structures hold a single actin, not a filament; actin is U-shaped with the nucleotide deep in the groove between the two arms.

sources.title: Molecule of the Month: DNA
sources.checked: Each cell carries about 1.5 gigabytes of genetic information; strands pair into the double helix; A pairs with T, G with C through hydrogen bonds; major and minor grooves expose chemical groups proteins read without unwinding; 1bna is the B form found in cells, bent at the top by crystal packing, with propeller twisted bases; Watson and Crick in the 1950s; proteins repair DNA corrupted by chemicals or radiation.

sources.title: Molecule of the Month: Green Fluorescent Protein (GFP)
sources.checked: From a jellyfish in the cold north Pacific; turns blue light from aequorin into green light; absorbs ultraviolet and emits green; attached to proteins or viruses to watch them in cells; chromophore built from three amino acids (serine or threonine, tyrosine, glycine) buried inside; oxygen finishes the chromophore over about an hour; 1ema: the chain forms a cylindrical can with a strand through the middle and the chromophore in the centre, shielded from water.

sources.title: Molecule of the Month: ATP Synthase
sources.checked: Builds most of the ATP in cells; two rotary motors, F0 in the membrane powered by hydrogen ions and F1 the chemical motor; F0 turns the rotor and axle and F1 becomes a generator making ATP; the axle forces F1 through three shapes: bind ADP and phosphate, make the bond, release ATP; the structure is solved in parts.

sources.title: Molecule of the Month: Aquaporin
sources.checked: Membranes resist water; kidneys and the eye use aquaporins to control water flow; four identical chains, each with its own channel; water passes single file; the red blood cell aquaporin; two asparagines hold a central water in a set orientation so the channel cannot pass protons; constriction controls what passes; mercury blocks water flow in red blood cells; blockers studied for glaucoma.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 1J6Z: Uncomplexed actin
sources.checked: Data API entry and local file: X-ray, 1.54 A, released 2001, Otterbein, Graceffa, Dominguez; rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus) actin alpha 1; one chain A with ADP, calcium ions and a tetramethylrhodamine dye; ADP phosphate held by calcium 382.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 1BNA: Structure of a B-DNA dodecamer
sources.checked: Data API entry and local file: X-ray, 1.9 A, 1981, Drew, Wing, Takano, Broka, Tanaka, Itakura, Dickerson; strand A residues 1 to 12 and strand B 13 to 24, sequence CGCGAATTCGCG.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 4HHB: The crystal structure of human deoxyhaemoglobin at 1.74 angstroms resolution
sources.checked: Data API entry and local file: X-ray, 1.74 A, 1984, Fermi, Perutz, Shaanan, Fourme; human; chains A and C alpha (141 residues), B and D beta (146 residues); one HEM per chain; iron bonded to His87 (alpha) and His92 (beta); beta residue 6 is GLU; phosphate ions on B and D.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 4INS: The structure of 2Zn pig insulin crystals at 1.5 angstroms resolution
sources.checked: Data API entry and local file: X-ray, 1.5 A, 1988 paper, Baker, Blundell, Cutfield, Dodson, Hodgkin and others; pig (Sus scrofa); A chains 1 to 21, B chains 1 to 30; disulfides A6 to A11, A7 to B7, A20 to B19; zinc bonded to His B10; B30 is alanine; two insulin molecules (A+B and C+D).

sources.title: RCSB PDB 1CAG: Crystal and molecular structure of a collagen-like peptide at 1.9 angstrom resolution
sources.checked: Data API entry and local file: X-ray, 1.85 A, 1994, Bella, Eaton, Brodsky, Berman; three chains A, B, C of 30 residues; repeat Pro-Hyp-Gly with alanine at A15, B45, C75 in place of glycine.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 1B7T: Myosin digested by papain
sources.checked: Data API entry and local file: X-ray, 2.5 A, 1999, Houdusse, Kalabokis, Himmel, Szent-Gyorgyi, Cohen; bay scallop (Argopecten irradians); chain A heavy chain with ADP and magnesium, chain Y regulatory light chain, chain Z essential light chain.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 1EMA: Green fluorescent protein from Aequorea victoria
sources.checked: Data API entry and local file: X-ray, 1.9 A, 1996, Ormo, Cubitt, Kallio, Gross, Tsien, Remington; one chain A; chromophore CRO is residue 66, joined to Phe64 and Val68; residue 203 is THR; selenomethionine at 78, 88, 153, 218.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 1LYZ: Real-space refinement of the structure of hen egg-white lysozyme
sources.checked: Data API entry and local file: X-ray, 2.0 A, 1974 paper by R. Diamond; chicken (Gallus gallus); one chain of 129 residues; disulfides 6 to 127, 30 to 115, 64 to 80, 76 to 94; residue 35 GLU, 52 ASP.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 1J4N: Crystal structure of the AQP1 water channel
sources.checked: Data API entry and local file: X-ray, 2.2 A, 2001, Sui, Han, Lee, Walian, Jap; cow (Bos taurus) aquaporin 1; one chain A, residues 1 to 249; Asn78, Asn194, His182 present.

sources.title: RCSB PDB 1MAB: Rat liver F1-ATPase
sources.checked: Data API entry and local file: X-ray, 2.8 A, 1998, Bianchet, Hullihen, Pedersen, Amzel; rat liver; the file holds one alpha chain (A, with ATP and magnesium), one beta chain (B, with ADP and phosphate) and the gamma chain (G); it is the F1 part only; biological assembly 1 is a heptamer of 3 alpha, 3 beta and 1 gamma (Data API assembly endpoint).

sources.title: Fermi G, Perutz MF, Shaanan B, Fourme R (1984) The crystal structure of human deoxyhaemoglobin at 1.74 A resolution. J Mol Biol 175:159-174
sources.publisher: Journal of Molecular Biology (abstract read on PubMed, PMID 6726807)
sources.checked: Abstract: refined at 1.74 A from synchrotron X-ray data; iron sits out of the heme plane in the deoxy form and is bonded to the F8 histidine nitrogen.

sources.title: Baker EN and others (1988) The structure of 2Zn pig insulin crystals at 1.5 A resolution. Phil Trans R Soc Lond B 319:369-456
sources.publisher: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B (abstract read on PubMed, PMID 2905485)
sources.checked: Abstract: 1.5 A X-ray data; two insulin molecules form a compact dimer and three dimers form a hexamer around two zinc ions.

sources.title: Bella J, Eaton M, Brodsky B, Berman HM (1994) Crystal and molecular structure of a collagen-like peptide at 1.9 A resolution. Science 266:75-81
sources.checked: Abstract: first protein triple helix at 1.9 A; each triple helix wrapped in a cylinder of water; hydroxyproline critical to the water network; Gly to Ala substitution locally untwists the helix and water bridges replace direct hydrogen bonds; similar Gly mutations in collagen cause osteogenesis imperfecta, chondrodysplasias and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome IV.

sources.title: Houdusse A, Kalabokis VN, Himmel D, Szent-Gyorgyi AG, Cohen C (1999) Atomic structure of scallop myosin subfragment S1 complexed with MgADP. Cell 97:459-470
sources.checked: Abstract: scallop striated muscle myosin head with MgADP at 2.5 A; converter and lever arm in a new position; likely a state before ATP is split in which the heads stay detached from actin.

sources.title: Ormo M, Cubitt AB, Kallio K, Gross LA, Tsien RY, Remington SJ (1996) Crystal structure of the Aequorea victoria green fluorescent protein. Science 273:1392-1395
sources.checked: Abstract: chromophore from cyclization and oxidation of Ser65 (or Thr65), Tyr66, Gly67; needs the native fold; Thr65 GFP at 1.9 A; 11-stranded beta barrel with a coaxial helix, chromophore formed from the central helix; changing Thr203 to Tyr or His shifts the colours toward red.

sources.title: Otterbein LR, Graceffa P, Dominguez R (2001) The crystal structure of uncomplexed actin in the ADP state. Science 293:708-711
sources.checked: Abstract: actin modified to block polymerization crystallized in the ADP state at 1.54 A; earlier ATP-actin structures came from complexes with DNase I, profilin and gelsolin; ADP-actin shows a marked change in subdomain 2.

sources.title: Drew HR, Wing RM, Takano T, Broka C, Tanaka S, Itakura K, Dickerson RE (1981) Structure of a B-DNA dodecamer: conformation and dynamics. PNAS 78:2179-2183
sources.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (abstract read on PubMed, PMID 6941276)
sources.checked: Abstract: synthetic dodecamer CGCGAATTCGCG at 1.9 A; slightly more than one full turn of right-handed B helix; 19 degree bend; 9.8 base pairs per turn in the centre; A.T pairs propeller twisted about 17.3 degrees, C.G pairs about 11.5.

sources.title: Sui H, Han BG, Lee JK, Walian P, Jap BK (2001) Structural basis of water-specific transport through the AQP1 water channel. Nature 414:872-878
sources.checked: Abstract: AQP1 at 2.2 A; extracellular and cytoplasmic vestibules joined by a long narrow pore; four bound waters in the selectivity filter; histidine 182 in the constriction is conserved in all water-specific channels and key to water specificity; proton transport through the channel is highly unfavourable; 10 aquaporin families AQP0 to AQP9 in mammals.

sources.title: Bianchet MA, Hullihen J, Pedersen PL, Amzel LM (1998) The 2.8-A structure of rat liver F1-ATPase. PNAS 95:11065-11070
sources.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (abstract read on PubMed, PMID 9736690)
sources.checked: Abstract: F1 is the part of ATP synthase with the catalytic and regulatory nucleotide sites; its shape changes couple proton flow to ATP synthesis; rat liver F1 at 2.8 A with physiological nucleotide levels; all three beta subunits hold nucleotide.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 2.2 Water
sources.checked: Polar covalent bonds, slightly positive hydrogens and slightly negative oxygen; hydrogen bonds between water molecules constantly form and break; dissolves polar molecules and ions; ice is less dense and floats; about 60 to 70 percent of the human body.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 3.2 Carbohydrates
sources.checked: Glucose is the most common monosaccharide, formula C6H12O6; energy from glucose in cellular respiration helps make ATP; plants make glucose from carbon dioxide and water; glucose, galactose and fructose are isomers.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 3.3 Lipids
sources.checked: Fatty acids are a hydrocarbon chain with a carboxyl group; palmitic acid is a saturated fatty acid named for the palm tree; saturated means only single bonds; animal fats with palmitic acid are common in meat; cells store long-term energy as fat; a phospholipid has two fatty acids on glycerol and phospholipids are major membrane parts; saturated fats might contribute to plaque in arteries; steroids have four linked carbon rings, cholesterol has a short tail and an OH group; liver makes cholesterol, precursor of steroid hormones, vitamin D and bile salts; LDL cholesterol plaque and heart disease.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 3.4 Proteins
sources.checked: Amino acid: central alpha carbon with amino group, carboxyl group, hydrogen and R group; glycine's R group is a hydrogen atom; 20 common amino acids; peptide bonds join them in a dehydration reaction; insulin has two chains A (21) and B (30) linked by disulfide bonds and regulates blood glucose; hemoglobin is globular, collagen fibrous; sickle cell is one amino acid change in the beta chain and the hemoglobin forms long fibers that make sickle-shaped cells.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 3.5 Nucleic Acids
sources.checked: DNA is the genetic material; double helix with sugar and phosphate backbone outside and bases inside; A pairs with T, G with C; base pairs 0.34 nm apart.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 4.5 The Cytoskeleton
sources.checked: Microfilaments are the narrowest cytoskeleton fibres, about 7 nm across, two intertwined strands of actin; ATP powers actin assembly; actin is a track for myosin; actin and myosin plentiful in muscle; filaments slide to contract muscle; microtubules about 25 nm.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 5.1 Components and Structure
sources.checked: Plasma membrane is phospholipids, cholesterol, proteins and carbohydrates; cholesterol of four fused carbon rings lies alongside the phospholipids and dampens temperature effects, extending the range where the membrane stays fluid.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 6.4 ATP: Adenosine Triphosphate
sources.checked: ATP is adenosine with three phosphate groups, named alpha, beta and gamma from the ribose outward; the bonds linking the phosphates are high-energy phosphoanhydride bonds; hydrolysis gives ADP and inorganic phosphate and releases energy; the reaction is reversible.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 7.4 Oxidative Phosphorylation
sources.checked: Hydrogen ions pass back through ATP synthase in the inner mitochondrial membrane; the ion current powers ATP synthase to add phosphate to ADP; ATP synthase uses the proton gradient to make ATP from ADP and phosphate; chemiosmosis.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 14.2 DNA Structure and Sequencing
sources.checked: Base pairs are 0.34 nm apart; one turn is 3.4 nm, so 10 base pairs per turn; the helix is 2 nm wide and uniform because a purine always pairs with a pyrimidine; strands antiparallel.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 22.2 Structure of Prokaryotes
sources.checked: A prokaryote's chromosome, usually single, is circular double-stranded DNA in an area of the cell called the nucleoid.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 37.3 Regulation of Body Processes
sources.checked: Insulin from pancreatic beta cells is released as blood glucose rises after a meal and lowers it by increasing glucose uptake; impaired insulin function leads to diabetes mellitus; type I diabetes is failure of the pancreas to produce insulin; ADH inserts aquaporins into kidney tubules so water moves out and urine volume falls.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 38.4 Muscle Contraction and Locomotion
sources.checked: Myosin heads bind actin and form cross-bridges that pull actin inward; myosin splits ATP to ADP and phosphate at its ATP site; the energy cocks the myosin head; ATP binding makes myosin release actin.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 40.2 Components of the Blood
sources.checked: Hemoglobin's iron makes blood red; two alpha and two beta chains with heme; each hemoglobin binds four oxygen molecules; about 250 million hemoglobin molecules per red blood cell, so each cell carries about one billion oxygen molecules; mammal red blood cells lack organelles leaving more room for hemoglobin.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 41.2 The Kidneys and Osmoregulatory Organs
sources.checked: The descending loop of Henle is lined with cells containing aquaporins that let water pass from the filtrate; water is also reabsorbed through aquaporins in the proximal tubule.

sources.title: UniProt P47865: Aquaporin-1 (Bos taurus)
sources.checked: 271 residues; six membrane-crossing helices (12 to 29, 49 to 67, 93 to 111, 136 to 155, 166 to 183, 209 to 226) and two half helices dipping into the membrane; NPA motifs at 78 to 80 and 194 to 196; forms a water channel; each half of the protein has three membrane-spanning parts and a pore-forming loop with the NPA signature.

sources.title: UniProt P00698: Lysozyme C (Gallus gallus)
sources.checked: Signal peptide 1 to 18, mature chain 19 to 147; active sites at 53 and 70 (Glu35 and Asp52 in the mature numbering used by 1LYZ); four disulfide bonds 24-145, 48-133, 82-98, 94-112 (6-127, 30-115, 64-80, 76-94 mature); bacteriolytic; found in egg white.

sources.title: UniProt P42212: Green fluorescent protein (Aequorea victoria)
sources.checked: 238 residues; turns the blue light of aequorin into green light by energy transfer; found in photocytes; chromophore from Ser65, Tyr66 and Gly67, formed by itself, needs only oxygen to mature.

sources.title: RCSB PDB Chemical Component Dictionary: PLM (palmitic acid)

sources.title: RCSB PDB Chemical Component Dictionary: CLR (cholesterol)
sources.checked: Local file data/CLR.cif: 27 carbons; rings C1-C2-C3-C4-C5-C10, C5-C6-C7-C8-C9-C10, C8-C9-C11-C12-C13-C14 and five-membered C13-C14-C15-C16-C17; O1 on C3; one C5=C6 double bond; tail C20 to C27 on C17.
